chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah, from Abī Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who prayed five [rak‘ahs]. He said: If he had sat in the fourth [rak‘ah] for the measure of the tashahhud, then his salat (prayer) is complete.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first two reports, because whoever sat in the fourth [rak‘ah] and recited the tashahhud, then stood and prayed an additional rak‘ah, has not omitted a pillar from the pillars of the salat (prayer). He only omitted the taslim, and omission of the taslim does not necessitate repeating the salat (prayer), according to what we have stated earlier.

key_terms.إِعَادَةَ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation ending the prayer
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in the sitting position near the end of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rak‘ah of the prayer
key_terms.بِرُكْنٍ: an essential pillar of the prayer whose omission invalidates it
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُهُ: his prayer is considered valid and complete
key_terms.صَلَّى خَمْسًا: prayed five rak‘ahs instead of the prescribed number

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone accidentally prays five rak‘ahs instead of four?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of one who unintentionally adds a fifth rak‘ah to a four-rak‘ah salat (prayer). If he had already sat in the fourth rak‘ah for the amount of tashahhud, the prayer is considered complete, because the addition did not invalidate an essential pillar, and omission of the taslim alone does not require repetition.
